Pooled application accuracy

Each observation is one device and one application input, compared with that device's own native reference; the same input on two devices is two observations.

Base and head comparison

Both rows use the same 723 qualified pooled observations with base and head predictions. The overview charts use all qualified head observations.

How every device view is built

Every device view has the same sections, drawn by the same code: application accuracy and timing curves, then the six diagnostic suites. A device with a native measurement of a suite shows it as the native series; a device without one shows the predictions on the same axes and says that nothing is compared with hardware. No device borrows another device's measurement. Instruction throughput is a table for every device on purpose: its probes are unrelated instruction mixes with one rate each and no shared axis. The paired capacity boundary is a separate native acquisition and is drawn only where it exists.

Memory latency, parallelism and bandwidth

Prediction only · no hardware comparison. No native NVIDIA Grace (Arm Neoverse V2) measurement of this suite exists. The points are simulator predictions on the suite's own axes: nothing is compared with hardware, no other device's measurement is shown and no accuracy is stated.

140 diagnostic points. Single-core scalar assembly; each short and long execution follows initialization and two full warmup passes. The total working set stays fixed across chain counts; Copy includes both buffers. These points do not enter application accuracy statistics.

One random chain measures dependent-load loop latency; multiple chains show aggregate time per load, not individual access latency. Streaming plots show effective scalar bytes/s, not cache-line or DRAM-bus traffic and not peak vector bandwidth. Sizes describe working sets, not verified physical cache levels. Base points absent because of image capacity are explicitly marked in the table.

Scheduling: complete · head 4/4; base 4/4 executions complete. No native reference exists for this device: predictions only.

Execution-unit scheduling probes

Prediction only · no hardware comparison. No native NVIDIA Grace (Arm Neoverse V2) measurement of this suite exists. The points are simulator predictions on the suite's own axes: nothing is compared with hardware, no other device's measurement is shown and no accuracy is stated.

Each iteration has eight blocks. Each block runs eight dependent MADD or FMADD updates, a dependent fan-out to six integer or four FP registers, then an optional independent eight-update ADD or FADD chain. A final join feeds both paths into the next block. The independent accumulator resets before each block. Instructions per iteration: int_chain: 130, int_interleaved: 194, fp_chain: 114, fp_interleaved: 178. Compare the incremental cost of independent work per iteration, not equal-instruction throughput. Simulation uses declared frequencies: base 3.429 GHz, head 3.429 GHz. These tested operand patterns do not establish physical M2 scheduling dimensions or arbitrary instruction latencies and are excluded from application accuracy statistics.

Capacity: complete · head 73/73; base 73/73 executions complete. No native reference exists for this device: predictions only.

FP capacity and divider controls

Prediction only · no hardware comparison. No native NVIDIA Grace (Arm Neoverse V2) measurement of this suite exists. The points are simulator predictions on the suite's own axes: nothing is compared with hardware, no other device's measurement is shown and no accuracy is stated.

Two independent integer dependency gates surround independent FP destinations. Gate lengths, NOP fillers and ungated FP throughput distinguish rename pressure from ROB, dependency and execution-port limits. Model ns use each profile’s assumed frequency to convert simulated cycles. The model FP destination cap is separate from its ROB capacity and is not a physical register-file size. Divider controls include trivial fixed points and normal reciprocal / sqrt(x+1) recurrences. All results remain separate from application accuracy statistics.

The paired capacity boundary (ABBA) is a separate native acquisition. None exists for NVIDIA Grace (Arm Neoverse V2), so that chart is not drawn here.

Forwarding: complete · head 13/13; base 13/13 executions complete. No native reference exists for this device: predictions only.

Store/load dependency probes

Prediction only · no hardware comparison. No native NVIDIA Grace (Arm Neoverse V2) measurement of this suite exists. The points are simulator predictions on the suite's own axes: nothing is compared with hardware, no other device's measurement is shown and no accuracy is stated.

Value-varying assembly updates; 64 updates per loop iteration. Hover a point for its values. Simulation converts cycles using the declared model frequency: base 3.429 GHz, head 3.429 GHz. These probes are excluded from application accuracy statistics.

Reg is the same-class register chain; direct uses immediate-offset load/store; apart is a nonoverlap throughput control, not a latency baseline. Idx uses register offsets on both sides, idx ld/st on one side. Compare/select increments and wraps modulo 65,536. Matched memory-minus-register differences estimate effective dependency cost including instruction/address overhead, not physical bypass latency. P10/P90 are variability summaries, not confidence intervals.

Recurrence: complete · head 41/41; base 41/41 executions complete. No native reference exists for this device: predictions only.

Compare/select and memory-recurrence probes

Prediction only · no hardware comparison. No native NVIDIA Grace (Arm Neoverse V2) measurement of this suite exists. The points are simulator predictions on the suite's own axes: nothing is compared with hardware, no other device's measurement is shown and no accuracy is stated.

Simulated values are model cycles per update. Hover a point for its values. These probes are excluded from application accuracy statistics.

Pair latency: W and X are 32- and 64-bit register compares selecting the compared registers, a adjacent, s with one instruction between, 8 and 4 the loop shifted by that many bytes (at 4 every fourth pair straddles a 64-byte line). Operand forms, all 32-bit and adjacent except 15s: swap selects the compared registers in the other order, dst writes a third register, other selects two registers that were not compared; 15r compares with immediate 15 and selects between the compared register and one other; 15a, 15s, 16a and shl compare with an immediate (15, 15, 16, 1 LSL 12) and select two registers that were not compared; inc uses CSINC. Mix is the independent compare/select/add/add stream. Store/load: same base register, a second base register holding the same address, displacement 8, a 32-bit load of a 64-bit store, no memory dependency, FP; near, mid and far reload 0, 4 and 8 instructions after the store; addr carries the recurrence through the load address. Maximum: constant or changing stored value and the separated pair; t is one static pair per taken branch (t same reloads into the register it stores); k is the eleven-instruction Nussinov loop replica. P10/P90 are variability summaries, not confidence intervals.

Memory latency, parallelism and bandwidth

Measured on Apple M1. Apple M1 Linux collection m1-7031aa3: thread CPU seconds of the simulated long-minus-short work, nine alternating pairs per point, logical CPU 4; P10 and P90 are the nearest lower ranks of the nine. Time comparison, not counted cycles. 140 of 140 points have a native time; any other point is a prediction only.

140 diagnostic points; 137 usable native references. Single-core scalar assembly; each short and long execution follows initialization and two full warmup passes. The total working set stays fixed across chain counts; Copy includes both buffers. These points do not enter application accuracy statistics.

One random chain measures dependent-load loop latency; multiple chains show aggregate time per load, not individual access latency. Streaming plots show effective scalar bytes/s, not cache-line or DRAM-bus traffic and not peak vector bandwidth. Sizes describe working sets, not verified physical cache levels. Noisy native points remain visible and are identified in every tooltip. Vertical ranges show native P10–P90 repeat variability, not confidence intervals or seed sensitivity. Base points absent because of image capacity are explicitly marked in the table.

Scheduling: complete · head 4/4; base 4/4 executions complete. This device's own native times are shown where it was measured; missing predictions are pending.

Execution-unit scheduling probes

Measured on Apple M1. Apple M1 Linux collection m1-7031aa3: thread CPU seconds of the simulated long-minus-short work, nine alternating pairs per point, logical CPU 4; P10 and P90 are the nearest lower ranks of the nine. Time comparison, not counted cycles. 4 of 4 points have a native time; any other point is a prediction only.

Each iteration has eight blocks. Each block runs eight dependent MADD or FMADD updates, a dependent fan-out to six integer or four FP registers, then an optional independent eight-update ADD or FADD chain. A final join feeds both paths into the next block. The independent accumulator resets before each block. Instructions per iteration: int_chain: 130, int_interleaved: 194, fp_chain: 114, fp_interleaved: 178. Compare the incremental cost of independent work per iteration, not equal-instruction throughput. Simulation uses declared frequencies: base 3.2035 GHz, head 3.2035 GHz. These tested operand patterns do not establish physical M2 scheduling dimensions or arbitrary instruction latencies and are excluded from application accuracy statistics.

Capacity: complete · head 73/73; base 73/73 executions complete. This device's own native times are shown where it was measured; missing predictions are pending.

FP capacity and divider controls

Measured on Apple M1. Apple M1 Linux collection m1-7031aa3: thread CPU seconds of the simulated long-minus-short work, nine alternating pairs per point, logical CPU 4; P10 and P90 are the nearest lower ranks of the nine. Time comparison, not counted cycles. 73 of 73 points have a native time; any other point is a prediction only.

Two independent integer dependency gates surround independent FP destinations. Gate lengths, NOP fillers and ungated FP throughput distinguish rename pressure from ROB, dependency and execution-port limits. Native ns are thread CPU-time differences; core and instantaneous frequency were unobserved. Model ns use each profile’s assumed frequency to convert simulated cycles. The model FP destination cap is separate from its ROB capacity and is not a physical register-file size. Divider controls include trivial fixed points and normal reciprocal / sqrt(x+1) recurrences. All results remain separate from application accuracy statistics.

The paired capacity boundary (ABBA) is a separate native acquisition. None exists for Apple M1, so that chart is not drawn here.

Forwarding: complete · head 13/13; base 13/13 executions complete. This device's own native times are shown where it was measured; missing predictions are pending.

Store/load dependency probes

Measured on Apple M1. Apple M1 Linux collection m1-7031aa3: thread CPU seconds of the simulated long-minus-short work, nine alternating pairs per point, logical CPU 4; P10 and P90 are the nearest lower ranks of the nine. Time comparison, not counted cycles. 13 of 13 points have a native time; any other point is a prediction only.

Value-varying assembly updates; 64 updates per loop iteration. Hover a point for its values. Simulation converts cycles using the declared model frequency: base 3.2035 GHz, head 3.2035 GHz. These probes are excluded from application accuracy statistics.

Reg is the same-class register chain; direct uses immediate-offset load/store; apart is a nonoverlap throughput control, not a latency baseline. Idx uses register offsets on both sides, idx ld/st on one side. Compare/select increments and wraps modulo 65,536. Matched memory-minus-register differences estimate effective dependency cost including instruction/address overhead, not physical bypass latency. P10/P90 are variability summaries, not confidence intervals.

Recurrence: complete · head 41/41; base 41/41 executions complete. This device's own native times are shown where it was measured; missing predictions are pending.

Compare/select and memory-recurrence probes

Measured on Apple M1. Apple M1 Linux collection m1-7031aa3: thread CPU seconds of the simulated long-minus-short work, nine alternating pairs per point, logical CPU 4; P10 and P90 are the nearest lower ranks of the nine. Time comparison, not counted cycles. 41 of 41 points have a native time; any other point is a prediction only.

Simulated values are model cycles per update. A native time is converted to cycles at the head profile's clock, 3.2035 GHz, which is an assumption about the measured core. Hover a point for its values. These probes are excluded from application accuracy statistics.

Pair latency: W and X are 32- and 64-bit register compares selecting the compared registers, a adjacent, s with one instruction between, 8 and 4 the loop shifted by that many bytes (at 4 every fourth pair straddles a 64-byte line). Operand forms, all 32-bit and adjacent except 15s: swap selects the compared registers in the other order, dst writes a third register, other selects two registers that were not compared; 15r compares with immediate 15 and selects between the compared register and one other; 15a, 15s, 16a and shl compare with an immediate (15, 15, 16, 1 LSL 12) and select two registers that were not compared; inc uses CSINC. Mix is the independent compare/select/add/add stream. Store/load: same base register, a second base register holding the same address, displacement 8, a 32-bit load of a 64-bit store, no memory dependency, FP; near, mid and far reload 0, 4 and 8 instructions after the store; addr carries the recurrence through the load address. Maximum: constant or changing stored value and the separated pair; t is one static pair per taken branch (t same reloads into the register it stores); k is the eleven-instruction Nussinov loop replica. P10/P90 are variability summaries, not confidence intervals.

Memory latency, parallelism and bandwidth

140 diagnostic points; 118 usable native references. Single-core scalar assembly; the same function instruction bytes run natively as Mach-O and in simulated ELF. Each short and long execution follows initialization and two full warmup passes. Native values use nine alternating long-minus-short thread CPU-time pairs. Core identity and instantaneous frequency were unobserved. The total working set stays fixed across chain counts; Copy includes both buffers. These points do not enter application accuracy statistics.

One random chain measures dependent-load loop latency; multiple chains show aggregate time per load, not individual access latency. Streaming plots show effective scalar bytes/s, not cache-line or DRAM-bus traffic and not peak vector bandwidth. Sizes describe working sets, not verified physical cache levels. Noisy native points remain visible and are identified in every tooltip. Vertical ranges show native P10–P90 repeat variability, not confidence intervals or seed sensitivity. Base points absent because of image capacity are explicitly marked in the table.

Execution-unit scheduling probes

Each iteration has eight blocks. Each block runs eight dependent MADD or FMADD updates, a dependent fan-out to six integer or four FP registers, then an optional independent eight-update ADD or FADD chain. A final join feeds both paths into the next block. The independent accumulator resets before each block. Instructions per iteration: int_chain: 130, int_interleaved: 194, fp_chain: 114, fp_interleaved: 178. Compare the incremental cost of independent work per iteration, not equal-instruction throughput. Native Apple M2 · 2026-11-08T03:37:04.810379+00:00. Nine alternating long-minus-short native macOS thread CPU-time pairs. Core and instantaneous frequency were unobserved; simulation uses declared frequencies: base 3.49 GHz, head 3.49 GHz. These tested operand patterns do not establish physical M2 scheduling dimensions or arbitrary instruction latencies and are excluded from application accuracy statistics.

FP capacity and divider controls

Two independent integer dependency gates surround independent FP destinations. Gate lengths, NOP fillers and ungated FP throughput distinguish rename pressure from ROB, dependency and execution-port limits. Native ns are thread CPU-time differences; core and instantaneous frequency were unobserved. Model ns use each profile’s assumed frequency to convert simulated cycles. The model FP destination cap is separate from its ROB capacity and is not a physical register-file size. Divider controls include trivial fixed points and normal reciprocal / sqrt(x+1) recurrences. All results remain separate from application accuracy statistics.

Post-acquisition deterministic analysis: gate 64: (366, 370]; gate 96: (366, 368]. Qualified counts ≤356 define each plateau: median of medians and maximum P90. A rise requires >15% above that median and P10 above the plateau maximum P90. Brackets run from the last qualified non-rise to the first qualified rise; noisy rows remain visible. The initial survey informed a dense confirmation sweep; quality and rise criteria were fixed before that second acquisition. Bars show sample P10–P90 dispersion, not confidence intervals.

Reg is the same-class register chain; direct uses immediate-offset load/store; apart is a nonoverlap throughput control, not a latency baseline. Idx uses register offsets on both sides, idx ld/st on one side. Compare/select increments and wraps modulo 65,536. Compare/select and memory-recurrence probes

Apple M2 · native Linux · marin-5 CPU 4, Linux 6.14.2-401.asahi.fc42.aarch64+16k, 16 KiB pages · pinned CPU 4; departures counted · 2026-11-10T13:30:54.628319+00:00. Cycles per update: user-mode cycle counter (perf_event). Counted instructions were 1.000001 of the declared loops and the counter advanced 3.4976 billion cycles per thread-CPU second. The counter group was enabled and running for the same 73.583 s, so it was never multiplexed. 12 mirrored blocks; each visit differences N and 2N trips in ABBA or BAAB order with intervals of about 24 ms or more. 100.0% of main intervals stayed on the reference core; other visits are counted, not mixed in. The operating system reported 3,504,000–3,504,000 kHz at block boundaries, an observation rather than a measurement. Simulated values are model cycles per update, so native and simulated points share one unit and no frequency is assumed. Hover a point for P10/median/P90, spread, quality and both simulator predictions. These probes are excluded from application accuracy statistics.

Pair latency: W and X are 32- and 64-bit register compares selecting the compared registers, a adjacent, s with one instruction between, 8 and 4 the loop shifted by that many bytes (at 4 every fourth pair straddles a 64-byte line). Operand forms, all 32-bit and adjacent except 15s: swap selects the compared registers in the other order, dst writes a third register, other selects two registers that were not compared; 15r compares with immediate 15 and selects between the compared register and one other; 15a, 15s, 16a and shl compare with an immediate (15, 15, 16, 1 LSL 12) and select two registers that were not compared; inc uses CSINC. Mix is the independent compare/select/add/add stream. Store/load: same base register, a second base register holding the same address, displacement 8, a 32-bit load of a 64-bit store, no memory dependency, FP; near, mid and far reload 0, 4 and 8 instructions after the store; addr carries the recurrence through the load address. Maximum: constant or changing stored value and the separated pair; t is one static pair per taken branch (t same reloads into the register it stores); k is the eleven-instruction Nussinov loop replica. P10/P90 are variability summaries, not confidence intervals.
